Primary Care Progress Note

Continue current medications and lifestyle. Routine monitoring and follow-up as scheduled. Patient advised to report any new symptoms promptly.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/18/2026
Patient: Gwyn Runolfsson, 71-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/18/2026: acute osteoporotic T12 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

No other acute abnormalities are identified in the thoracic or lumbar spine.

Impression:
Acute osteoporotic compression fracture at T12 with associated bone marrow edema, consistent with recent injury.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician based on clinical findings.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/25/2026
Patient: Gwyn Runolfsson, 71-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 08/22/2026 after a fall from standing height, 5 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Current Status:
Pain now NRS 2/10 with acetaminophen and calcitonin nasal spray and bracing. Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and bracing. Monitor symptoms closely and follow up as needed for further intervention.
